title: How the US Federal Reserve reaches markets
text: The US Fed influences global liquidity and the dollar, so its decisions are watched by markets worldwide, including India. Reactions depend on how the decision compares with what markets expected.

title: Why the ECB matters beyond Europe
text: Decisions by the ECB can influence the euro, global bond yields and overall risk sentiment, which is one channel through which they reach other markets.

title: How interest rates reach the market
text: Interest rates set the cost of borrowing. Higher rates tend to raise costs for borrowers and make fixed-income options more attractive compared with stocks, while lower rates work the other way. Rate-sensitive sectors such as banks, NBFCs and real estate are watched closely.

title: Why inflation data is watched
text: Inflation shows how fast prices are rising. Central banks watch it when deciding interest rates, so inflation data often matters to markets through the interest rate path.

title: How crude oil prices reach the market
text: India imports most of its crude oil, so oil prices feed into import costs, inflation and the rupee. Different sectors feel it differently, for example oil marketers, airlines and paint companies.

title: How the rupee and the dollar matter
text: A weaker rupee tends to raise import costs and help exporters, while a stronger rupee tends to do the opposite. Currency moves also influence foreign investor flows.

title: Why bond yields are watched
text: Bond yields are the return on government bonds. Rising yields can raise borrowing costs and make equities look relatively less attractive, which is why the link is followed closely around the world.

title: What growth data tells markets
text: Growth data shows how fast the economy is expanding. Over time it shapes expectations for company earnings and for which sectors may be doing better or worse.

title: How trade duties work through markets
text: Duties change the cost of goods moving across borders. They usually affect specific sectors and companies first, with wider effects depending on their size and scope.

title: Why foreign investor flows matter
text: Foreign investor buying and selling is a large source of market liquidity. Sustained flows in either direction can influence index levels and the rupee.

title: How company results reach the index
text: Company results update expectations about profits. Large companies carry more weight in the indices, so their results can matter more for index moves than those of smaller ones.

title: Why government spending and tax policy matter
text: Government spending and tax decisions shape growth expectations and sector outlooks. Markets also follow the fiscal deficit and borrowing plans because they influence bond yields.

title: What banking liquidity changes
text: Liquidity measures change how much money is available in the banking system. This influences short-term interest rates and the ease with which banks can lend.

title: How SEBI rules shape the market
text: Rule changes by the market regulator can alter how brokers, exchanges and investors operate, for example margin, disclosure and product rules.

title: Why gold is followed
text: Gold is often followed as a safe-haven asset. Its price is linked to the dollar, interest rates and import demand.

title: How geopolitical events reach markets
text: Geopolitical events add uncertainty. Markets often respond to uncertainty with higher volatility, and the effects on oil, currencies and sentiment are commonly watched.
